title: Decision Space Decomposition for Multiobjective Optimization
headline: Open finding: Proposition 2.5 is false as printed; a continuous map with globally strictly convex components violates the asserted inverse-image convergence.

work.title: Decision Space Decomposition for Multiobjective Optimization
work.venue: Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications

claims.label: Proposition 2.5 inverse-image convergence claim
claims.gist: Proposition 2.5 asserts that continuity of f alone preserves Painlevé–Kuratowski convergence under inverse images.
claims.statement: For every continuous f:R^n→R^p, Painlevé–Kuratowski convergence Y_N→Y implies Painlevé–Kuratowski convergence f⁻¹(Y_N)→f⁻¹(Y).
conditions: The map is continuous; the proposition is stated for all continuous maps and convergent image sets.
claims.quantifiers: The claim is universal over continuous f and sequences Y_N with Painlevé–Kuratowski limit Y.

result.summary: A continuous map with globally strictly convex components and nonempty singleton image sets gives Y_N→Y in Hausdorff distance, while the inverse images converge to {1} and the limiting inverse image is {−1,1}. The lower-limit inclusion fails.
result.witness: Let F(x)=(x²,g(x)), where g(x)=x⁴+x²+x³−x. Both components are globally strictly convex. For N≥2, put x_N=1−1/N, Y_N={F(x_N)}, and Y={F(1)}={(1,2)}. Then Y_N→Y even in Hausdorff distance. For every finite N, F⁻¹(Y_N)={1−1/N}, so F⁻¹(Y_N)→{1}; but F⁻¹(Y)={−1,1}. Thus −1 in F⁻¹(Y) cannot be approached by points in F⁻¹(Y_N). The witness has nonempty singleton image sets and finite nonempty inverse images; it uses neither an empty set nor a constant map.
result.argument: The first coordinate forces any preimage of F(x_N) to be ±x_N. The second coordinate distinguishes these values for each finite N, while F(−1)=F(1)=(1,2). Thus the inverse image at each finite index is a singleton tending to {1}, but the limiting inverse image also contains −1. This violates the Painlevé–Kuratowski lower-limit inclusion and refutes Proposition 2.5 as printed. Proposition 5.3 invokes Proposition 2.5 and Proposition 5.5 cites Proposition 5.3; these are downstream proof dependencies requiring reanalysis only.
not_claimed: A corrected general theorem has been established.
The authors agree with the finding.
